items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What about Schofi and Leon Prima? ... INTERVIEWEE: It was, uh, a dance band... And that's where I played with, uh, Skiro. He had that job out there. The butcher I mentioned. Joe Skiro.

ctx.x: Yes. Yes. Wade was in the Eastern Band too. So was Godfrey Hirsch. You see, as you're unconscious of these things come back to you. But Godfrey was a perennial student. Godfrey stayed at Warren Easton for six years, you know. I think he liked the atmosphere. And then he went to Tulane for about another 27. Yeah. And he played in the Tulaneans. Tell us about the Tulaneans. I don't know what you bought him. I didn't, I didn't work with that band. Godfrey played with that band. That was another, just a name to me.…
a trombone, clarinet. No. What about Schofi and Leon Prima? What kind of band was that?

It was, uh, a dance band. Again, we had three saxes, three brass, and four rhythm. Uh, this was in the day of the open air dance hall. The first one that I remember was the old Frolics on St. Anne Street, just a few feet away from Broad, North Broad. And that's where I played with, uh, Skiro. He had that job out there.
